# 1 Clement Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_002_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 2

**2:1** All were given a profound and rich peace, and an insatiable desire to do good, and a full outpouring of the Holy Spirit was upon all.

**2:2** Being full of holy purpose, with excellent zeal and a pious eagerness, you stretched out your hands to God Almighty, beseeching him to be propitious, if you had inadvertently transgressed anything.

**2:3** Day and night you were earnest on behalf of the whole brotherhood, that the number of his elect might be saved with mercy and a good conscience.

**2:4** You were sincere and innocent and free from malice toward one another.

**2:5** Every faction and every schism was abominable to you. You mourned over the transgressions of your neighbors. You judged their shortcomings as your own.

**2:6** You were free from regret regarding every good work. You were ready for every good work.

**2:7** Being adorned with a most virtuous and honorable way of life, you performed all things in his fear. The commandments and ordinances of the Lord were inscribed on the tablets of your hearts.

---

*EMET renders with maximal literalness, preserving Greek word order where intelligible.*
